_doc: A kid on a bicycle at the crossroads, mornings and dusks, ten or so, with bones in the bike basket and a mamaw who says the water-tower owl is the 1955 owl's ghost. Trust 1, eager, not allowed out after the streetlight and out after it anyway. The red check gets what he saw come down; the farm kid's confession about the porch posts is the evidence way in.

open.speaker: kc_kid
lines: Y'all the ones from the paper? Y'all got a camera? Mamaw says don't talk to the paper but y'all ain't got a van so.
I know where it eats. The owl. There's bones. I can show you for a dollar, or for nothing if you let me look in the car.
I'm going to let him look in the car.

passives.line: A cat's jawbone and three owl pellets in the bike basket, picked clean and sorted by size. He's been collecting under that tower for weeks. Careful, too.
He said 'when the streetlight comes on' like a boy who's supposed to be indoors by then and isn't. Mamaw's rule. He's broken it.

options.text: You can look in the car. What's your name?
A dollar. Everybody in Kelly's got a price, and yours is the fairest yet.
Does your mamaw know where you are?

hub.speaker: kc_kid
lines: Okay. Okay. What else. I know everything. Ask me.

static.line: He was out after the streetlight and he saw it come down. He's ten. He'll say anything to a grown-up who says 'I believe you'. Say it.

options.text: A ghost owl. Does it eat ghost cats?
Who told you about 1955? Not your mamaw. Somebody at the store.

fail.line: Everybody. Everybody tells it. You can't buy a Grapette without it. Ask me something hard.

options.text: Show us where it eats. Properly, the way a scout would. Which side of the tower, which way the wind was.
You've been out after the streetlight. You saw it come down off the tower. Tell us, and nobody tells your mamaw.
The kid out at the farm says you two shot the porch posts. With a .410. Last month.
That's all for now. Go home before the streetlight.

name.speaker: kc_kid
lines: Travis. Travis Keel. Buford on the porch is my great-uncle. He seen one. It waved at him.
Mamaw says Uncle Buford seen a scarecrow. I ain't decided. I'm collecting evidence. That's what y'all do, right? That's what the bones is.
Ten years old and he's already got a better method than the Ledger.

ghost_cats.speaker: kc_kid
lines: No, it eats real cats. That's how you know it's real and a ghost both. Mr Hardin's Smoky. I found his collar.
I didn't tell Mr Hardin about the collar.
Mamaw says owls live twenty years and this is a hundred-year owl so it's got to be a ghost. I looked it up.
Great horned, twenty-eight in a zoo. So maybe it's the grandbaby.
That's still the same owl, kind of. Right?

store_version.speaker: kc_kid
lines: Mr Oates. At the store, when it's slow. He don't tell it like Uncle Buford. He tells it like it's a thing that happened to people.
He says the Lacys was scared and there was eleven of them and the babies cried all night. He says don't ever laugh at it.
He says he sold them ice in the morning and their hands shook.
Then he says go on home, Travis, and I go. He's the only one makes me go.

midden.speaker: kc_kid
lines: Okay. North leg of the tower, 'cause the wind's out of the south in summer and it sits on the lee side. Pellets right under the crossbar.
Bones is further out where it drops 'em.
Fresh ones is black and shiny. Old ones is grey and fall apart. There's a fresh one every morning so it's eating every night. Big ones.
The cat was a big one.
I put a stick in the ground every day I find one. There's forty-one sticks.
Forty-one days of pellets, dated, on the lee side of a known roost. I'd hire him.

midden_no.speaker: kc_kid
lines: ...It's up there. Right now. It's looking at us. Don't look.
I'll show you tomorrow. In the morning. It sleeps in the morning. I got to go.

came_down.speaker: kc_kid
lines: It came off the crossbar and it didn't flap, it just opened up and came down the light, big as a door, and its eyes was on. On.
Like the light was coming out of them.
It went over my head so close I felt it. It didn't make no sound.
Then it was on the Hardin fence with something, and the something was crying.
I rode home so fast I wrecked. Mamaw thinks I wrecked on the gravel. That's the only lie I ever told her.
Big as a door, silent, eyes lit, hands up in the headlight. He just told us the Lacy porch in 1955, and he's ten, and it's true.

came_down_no.speaker: kc_kid
lines: I ain't been out after the streetlight. Mamaw'd skin me. Who said?
...I got to go. Y'all can look at the bones yourself. North leg.

posts.speaker: kc_kid
lines: It was his .410. It was his idea. He said the tourists want new holes and his uncle would charge more. I only shot the one post.
The low one. He shot the rest.
Don't tell Mr Oates. Mr Oates would stop telling me it.
Fresh pellet scars in the porch posts, explained by two boys and a .410. I'll take that off the board tonight.
